statement: For $f(x)=\ln(x+1)$, find $f'(x)$ and the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$, and verify that $f(f^{-1}(x))=x$.
solution: $f'(x)=\dfrac{1}{x+1}$. To invert: $y=\ln(x+1)\Rightarrow x+1=e^{y}\Rightarrow x=e^{y}-1$, so $f^{-1}(x)=e^{x}-1$. Then $f(f^{-1}(x))=\ln((e^{x}-1)+1)=\ln(e^{x})=x$.
hints: Swap $x$ and $y$ and solve for $y$ to get the inverse.
